newsitem.title: FINLAND: LIPPONEN'S EMU THINK-TANK NOT TO RECOMMEND YES/NO.
newsitem.headline: LIPPONEN'S EMU THINK-TANK NOT TO RECOMMEND YES/NO.

text.p: An expert committee appointed by Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen to review pros and cons of Finnish participation in EMU will not take a stance for or against membership, the committee chairman said on Thursday.
"The group will not make recommendations for or against Finnish membership," economics professor Jukka Pekkarinen told a news conference.
"We will not present numerical estimates, for example the effect on GDP of Finnish EMU membership," he added.
Lipponen appointed the committee on November 28 to examine the effects of the planned third stage of Europe's Economic and Monetary Union on the Finnish economy.
Pekkarinen said the committee would pay particular attention to the structure of production, labour markets and economic policy.
The group's first medium-term report is due in March and the actual report will be presented in May next year.
Pekkarinen said the committee members would not make comments in public before the publication of the report.

The studies compiled by the Pekkarinen group are among many EMU-related reports due for publication before parliament decides, late in 1997 or early in 1998, whether Finland should join the third stage of EMU among the first countries in 1999.
The Finnish Institute of International Affairs is due to publish a study on the political aspects of EMU by March.
That study is part of a series of reports funded by the trade and industry ministry, and contributions will come from Finnish and foreign researchers.
